localChanges: All 62 packages are published and pushed. A clean reinstall resolves every one at its new version, with zero drift in the 263 packages Stage 1 never touched, and the conformance checksums are unchanged against the published artifacts — 7d6b6b04 / 73a0cc05 / 3431063b, as before.
Committing the lockfile because it is now the record of which versions were verified together, which is what 04-package-workflow.md asks for and what a bisect would need.
`pnpm-workspace.yaml` carries the settings that make `pnpm install` work at all on pnpm 11, each earned from a failure:
`overrides` restored from the lockfile, which recorded pins no config declared any more (ERR_PNPM_LOCKFILE_CONFIG_MISMATCH)
`blockExoticSubdeps: false`, because 22 of these packages are `github:` declared and depend on each other that way (ERR_PNPM_EXOTIC_SUBDEP)

`minimumReleaseAge: 0`, because pnpm 11 refuses very recently published versions and ours were minutes old. This one failed silently: resolution quietly chose the previous version of all 62 while the registry had the new ones, so a conformance run would have tested the old code and passed.
`allowBuilds` filled in, replacing the placeholders pnpm wrote itself
`glob` moves into devDependencies: `buildPluginList.js` has always required it without declaring it, and was resolving through hoisting that a clean install no longer provides.

`should be possible to get yields via `tilesWorked`` asserted that a city built with a bare `RuleRegistry` works one tile, but nothing in this package ever creates a `WorkedTile` — the rules that do live in `core-city-growth` and the `civ1-*` plugins. So `tilesWorked()` read the shared `WorkedTileRegistry` singleton and found whatever happened to be in it, which in a clean run is nothing. The assertion has been failing deterministically, and predates the `#private` conversion.

The test now takes its own `WorkedTileRegistry`, passes it to the city, and registers the centre tile, so it exercises `tilesWorked()` rather than depending on global state. `setUpCity` gained the matching optional parameter.

`Interaction._turn` is `protected` rather than `private`: `Declaration` declared its own `#turn` shadowing it, which two `private` fields of the same name cannot express. Merging the slots changes nothing, as `Interaction` reads `_turn` only in its constructor, before `Declaration` can assign to it.
